# Welcome to the `propopbirth` package

Birth rate forecasts based on FSO (Federal Statistical Office)
methodology

## Overview

The [propopbirth](https://github.com/statistik-aargau/propopbirth)
package consists of three modules: First, model input data are
calculated. Second, **TFR (total fertility rate)** and **MAB (mean age
of the mother at birth)** are predicted. Third, TFR and MAB forecasts
are used to predict the **age-specific birth rates**.

## Population projections

The output from
[propopbirth](https://github.com/statistik-aargau/propopbirth) is fully
compatible with
[`{propop} - An R package for population projections in R`](https://statistik-aargau.github.io/propop/index.html).
`{propop}` needs future birth rates as input. This is only available at
the FSO at cantonal level.
[propopbirth](https://github.com/statistik-aargau/propopbirth) can also
calculate birth rates for other spatial units or with own hypothesis.

## Installation

To install the current github version of the package, make sure you have
devtools installed and type:

``` r

devtools::install_github("statistik-aargau/propopbirth")
```

## Vignettes

The package includes three vignettes.

- Vignette 1: Prepare **model** **input data** from birth and
  population, with **examples**
- Vignette 2: **Forecast of** **TFR** (total fertility rate) and **MAB**
  (mean age of the mother at birth), with **examples**
- Vignette 3: Forecast of the **age-specific fertility rate**; including
  an **example of the complete forecast** of the age-specific birth rate

## Limitations, future plans

### Limitations

With population scenario models, it is always necessary to check whether
the spatial units are large enough to ensure that **meaningful forecast
estimates**. There is no population limit specification by the FSO, when
not to run the forecast models. However, it **visual checks** are
advisable (see vignette graphs for examples). These are helpful to
verify whether the estimates for the birth rate forecasts are
meaningful.

### Future plans

Currently, FSO birth data is not accessible with the required variables.
For this reason, the birth data (up to year 2023) is included in the
[propopbirth](https://github.com/statistik-aargau/propopbirth) package.
As soon as the birth data is publicly accessible (similar to population
data), it will be directly accessible in
[propopbirth](https://github.com/statistik-aargau/propopbirth) . This
will allow a more flexible selection of spatial units (not only
municipalities, but also districts).

## Examples

Detailed examples with explanations are provided in the vignettes (step
by step). This is an example of entire birth rate forecast for three
municipalities:

### Birth and population data

``` r

library(propopbirth)
library(dplyr)
```

### Create model input data

``` r

input <- create_input_data(
  population = fso_pop,
  births = fso_birth |> 
    dplyr::filter(spatial_unit %in% c("Aarau", "Uster", "Stadt Zürich")),
  year_first = 2011,
  year_last = 2023,
  age_fert_min = 15,
  age_fert_max = 49,
  fert_hist_years = 3,
  binational = TRUE
) 
```

### TFR (total fertility rate) forecast

``` r

forecast_tfr <- forecast_tfr_mab(
  topic = "tfr",
  topic_data = input$tfr,
  trend_model = c(
    model = "lm", start = 2024, end = 2026, trend_past = 7, trend_prop = 0.5
  ),
  temporal_model = c(
    model = "cubic", start = 2027, end = 2055, trend_prop = 0.8, z0_prop = 0.7,
    z1_prop = 0
  ),
  temporal_end = NA,
  constant_model = c(model = "constant", start = 2056, end = 2075)
)
```

### MAB (mean age of the mother at birth) forecast

``` r

forecast_mab <- forecast_tfr_mab(
  topic = "mab",
  topic_data = input$mab,
  trend_model = c(
    model = "lm", start = 2024, end = 2026, trend_past = 7, trend_prop = 0.5
  ),
  temporal_model = c(
    model = "Bezier", start = 2027, end = 2055, trend_prop = 0.3, z0_prop = 0.7,
    z1_prop = 0
  ),
  temporal_end = NA,
  constant_model = c(model = "constant", start = 2056, end = 2075)
) 
```

### Forecast of the age-specific fertility rate

``` r

forecast_fer <- forecast_fertility_rate(
  fer_dat = input$fer,
  tfr_dat = forecast_tfr,
  mab_dat = forecast_mab, 
  year_begin = 2024, 
  year_end = 2075)
```

## Acknowledgment

We acknowledge the Federal Statistical Office (FSO) for providing their
SAS code used for fertility projections. And we are grateful to the FSO
for giving the permission to use the birth data within the
[propopbirth](https://github.com/statistik-aargau/propopbirth) package.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`create_input_data()`](https://statistik-aargau.github.io/propopbirth/reference/create_input_data.md)
  : Create model input data
- [`forecast_fertility_rate()`](https://statistik-aargau.github.io/propopbirth/reference/forecast_fertility_rate.md)
  : Forecast age-specific fertility rates.
- [`forecast_tfr_mab()`](https://statistik-aargau.github.io/propopbirth/reference/forecast_tfr_mab.md)
  : Forecast total fertility rate (TFR) or mean age of the mother at
  birth (MAB)
- [`fso_birth`](https://statistik-aargau.github.io/propopbirth/reference/fso_birth.md)
  : FSO data for births
- [`fso_pop`](https://statistik-aargau.github.io/propopbirth/reference/fso_pop.md)
  : Population data from the Federal Statistical Office
- [`get_population_data()`](https://statistik-aargau.github.io/propopbirth/reference/get_population_data.md)
  : Get FSO population (females at 'fertile' age)
